open_points.subject: Flow composition and proof of node references
open_points.text: A05 says the proof checks whether “a function node names an existing contract version” and whether an operation node names an accepted binding, and keeps every otherwise well-formed version; A16 says a request naming any nonexistent record is refused as an unknown reference “never as a proof failure”.
open_points.question: Is a structurally valid flow version containing an unknown contract version or binding kept with a phase-1 proof failure, or refused before the version is kept?
options: Keep it and return a phase-1 proof failure
Refuse composition as an unknown reference and keep nothing
open_points.default_guess: Refuse it before keeping anything, following A16.

open_points.subject: Implementation submission and activation
open_points.text: M09 says kernel activation occurs “on a new admitted verdict”, while A04 says an existing verdict for the current corpus is reused and every admitted verdict is followed by activation unless that implementation is already current.
open_points.question: When an old admitted implementation is resubmitted while another implementation is current, does reuse of its cached verdict reactivate it automatically?
options: Reactivate it from the cached admitted verdict
Return the existing implementation and verdict without changing activation
Require the explicit rollback action
open_points.default_guess: Reactivate it, following A04 rules 2 and 4.

open_points.subject: Run authority for draft-write effects
open_points.text: M26 records “the flow activation under which the run started” as authority, but M19 pins only the flow version and function implementations, not the particular FlowActivation record.
open_points.question: How is the exact FlowActivation under which a run started identified later, especially after the same version has been activated more than once?
options: Store the FlowActivation position on the Run
Derive it from the latest activation preceding the Run in store order
Use whichever activation of that version is current when the send occurs
open_points.default_guess: Store the exact FlowActivation position on the Run at start.

open_points.subject: Disclosure class of an empty mapped result
open_points.text: A13 says an empty mapped output “takes the class of the list the node mapped over”, while A07 says a function output takes the highest class actually received and that no flow construct lowers a class. A mapped node may also have higher-class broadcast inputs.
open_points.question: What class does an empty mapped output receive when another input to the mapped node has a higher class than the empty mapped list?
options: The highest class among all node inputs
Only the class of the mapped-over list
The proof-time maximum class for the output
open_points.default_guess: Use the highest class among all inputs supplied to the mapped node.

open_points.subject: Authored trial-case input and expected-output shape
open_points.text: A04 requires that inputs and expected outputs “fit” their ports and mentions per-port presence checks, but does not say whether extra entries are refused or whether present expected_outputs may name only a subset of output ports.
open_points.question: Must trial inputs name exactly every input port, and must present expected_outputs name exactly every output port rather than a subset?
options: Inputs must be exact; expected_outputs is either absent or exact
Inputs must be exact; expected_outputs may be partial
Both maps may be partial where named values fit
open_points.default_guess: Require exact inputs and either absent or exact expected outputs.

open_points.subject: Admission persistence and crash recovery
open_points.text: A04 says admission records one TrialExecution per case, then a verdict, then an immediate activation, while A18 only says each store change is one transaction and does not identify the transaction boundaries for admission.
open_points.question: After a crash during admission or between its verdict and activation, which partial records may remain, and does startup resume, discard or leave that admission for a later submission?
options: Trial executions may remain; no verdict is created until all finish; a later submission starts a new admission
The whole admission including activation is atomic
Persist progress and resume the same admission after restart
open_points.default_guess: Keep completed TrialExecutions as observations, create verdict and activation atomically only after all cases finish, and require resubmission after interruption.

open_points.subject: Composite store changes
open_points.text: K-17 and A18 say “a change is one call in one transaction”, but the texts do not say which records form one change for operations that create several records, such as slot plus first contract, flow plus first version, run plus pins and inputs, or verdict plus activation.
open_points.question: Which groups of records must commit atomically, and which intermediate states are permitted after a store failure?
options: Define an atomic group for every surface action or execution stage
Commit each record separately and recover all intermediate states
Make each entire surface request one transaction
open_points.default_guess: Use explicit logical-stage transactions: creation pairs together, run creation with all pins, and verdict with its automatic activation.

open_points.subject: Sandbox clock prohibition
open_points.text: K-02 and A03 describe functions as having no clock, but A03's closed trapped list omits other CPython 3.12 clock or timing interfaces such as time.clock_gettime, os.times and resource usage readings.
open_points.question: Are unlisted timing interfaces intentionally usable in release v1, or must every observable clock and timing source be blocked?
options: Only the enumerated entry points are blocked
All clock and timing sources are forbidden even if omitted from the list
The product promise is only that common wall-clock APIs are blocked
open_points.default_guess: Treat all observable clock and timing sources as forbidden and issue a corrected release list.

open_points.subject: Determinism of function executions
open_points.text: A03 requires the same implementation and input to yield the same output digest, but code may observe values not covered by the traps, such as process identifiers, object identities, filesystem metadata or resource counters.
open_points.question: Which observable runtime facts besides clock and randomness must be hidden or stabilized to make repeatable output enforceable?
options: Hide or stabilize every nondeterministic observable
Permit such observables and drop the repeatability guarantee
Detect nondeterminism by repeated trials
open_points.default_guess: Hide or stabilize all nondeterministic observables exposed by the sandbox runtime.

open_points.subject: Sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input”, while A03 gives it an exchange directory and explicitly permits opening paths inside that directory without defining which files or writes user code may access.
open_points.question: May function code create and inspect arbitrary temporary files in the exchange directory, or may it access only runner-managed input and output objects?
options: Allow arbitrary ephemeral scratch access within the bounded directory
Expose only specific input and output paths
Expose no filesystem API to user code because files are passed as bytes
open_points.default_guess: Expose only runner-managed data and a separately bounded scratch area with explicit semantics.

open_points.subject: Sandbox audit hook and process creation
open_points.text: A03 says the audit hook raises on “subprocess”, but its required test expects a fork loop to reach process_count and end resource_exhausted rather than sandbox_violation.
open_points.question: Which exact audit events and process APIs are forbidden, and is bare fork allowed while exec, posix_spawn and subprocess creation are forbidden?
options: Allow fork but forbid execution of external programs
Forbid all child-process creation
Allow all process creation up to process_count
open_points.default_guess: Allow bare fork so the stated test is possible, but forbid exec and external-program spawning through an explicit event/API list.

open_points.subject: Sandbox resource-limit outcomes
open_points.text: A03 says “a limit hit” for memory, process count, scratch or output decides resource_exhausted, even if user code may receive and catch MemoryError or OSError, and it does not define what bytes or processes count.
open_points.question: What observable condition constitutes each limit being hit, whether a caught allocation or fork failure still counts, and whether process_count includes the runner and all descendants?
options: Any kernel-enforced denial is recorded and forces resource_exhausted even if caught
Only termination or measured excess counts
The caught exception may be handled and the execution may succeed
open_points.default_guess: Record every enforcement denial out of band and force resource_exhausted; count the runner and all descendants.

open_points.subject: Sandbox stdout, stderr and diagnostic channels
open_points.text: A03 says stdout is never kept and failure_detail is bounded, but does not say where stdout and stderr go or bound the bytes sent from the runner before truncation.
open_points.question: How are stdout, stderr and arbitrarily large exception messages drained and bounded so code cannot block the runner or exhaust the host?
options: Redirect stdout and stderr to a bounded discard sink and bound runner diagnostics before transfer
Capture them up to failure_detail_bytes_max
Inherit the kernel process streams
open_points.default_guess: Drain stdout and stderr to a bounded discard sink and cap diagnostic transfer before it reaches the parent.

open_points.subject: Many-file function outputs
open_points.text: A03 counts only the sum of file-content bytes for a many file output, while each element creates spool and trace metadata; an arbitrarily large list of empty files can therefore remain within output_bytes.
open_points.question: What bounds the number and metadata size of files in a many file output?
options: Count canonical framing and metadata toward output_bytes
Add a release ceiling for file count
Accept any count that fits sandbox memory
open_points.default_guess: Count the complete serialized output description, including per-file metadata, toward output_bytes.

open_points.subject: MCP transport and token carriage
open_points.text: A16 says every MCP request carries one token and request size is “the bytes of the request message as received”, but no MCP transport, token location or counted framing is specified.
open_points.question: Which MCP transport is used, where is the token carried, and which encoded bytes—including or excluding transport headers and framing—count toward surface_request_bytes_max?
options: Specify one HTTP-based MCP transport and an authorization header
Specify stdio or another framed transport with a token field
Treat transport choice and byte accounting as adapter-defined
open_points.default_guess: Use one specified MCP transport, carry the token in its authentication metadata, and count the decoded MCP request message including its token field.

open_points.subject: Agent-token configuration reload
open_points.text: M27 says repeated agent names make configuration invalid, but A16 says exactly three checks apply on token-list reread: parseability, minimum token length and token uniqueness. It does not recheck unique names or define conflicting may-author values.
open_points.question: Can a live reload introduce two agents with the same name or ambiguous author rights, and if not, which validation rejects it?
options: Apply all Actor/token-list invariants on every reload
Apply only the three listed checks and permit duplicate names
Reject changes to names or author rights until restart
open_points.default_guess: Apply unique agent names and unambiguous may-author values on every token-list reload.

open_points.subject: Configuration reload snapshot
open_points.text: A16 compares a hash of configuration bytes and then “re-reads” the file, without saying that hashing and parsing use one immutable byte snapshot if the file changes during the request.
open_points.question: Which bytes determine both the change test and the token list when the configuration file is replaced or rewritten during a request?
options: Read once into an immutable byte buffer, then hash and parse that buffer
Hash and parse separate reads and retry if they differ
Require atomic host-side replacement and leave races unspecified
open_points.default_guess: Read one bounded immutable snapshot and use it for both hashing and parsing.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision access
open_points.text: M28 and A08 require reading <manifest_location>/<service_id>.json “at the configured manifest_revision”, but do not define how a repository revision is resolved or how symlinks and paths inside that revision are handled.
open_points.question: How does the kernel read an exact revision without depending on the working tree, and may a manifest entry at that revision be a symbolic link?
options: Read blobs directly from the repository object database and reject symlinks
Require manifest_location to be an already materialized immutable snapshot
Read the working tree and merely record the configured revision
open_points.default_guess: Read the file blob directly at the exact repository revision and reject non-regular entries and symlinks.

open_points.subject: Service credential references
open_points.text: A17 calls a credential source “the reference that resolves to its value on the host” and later mentions a secret file, but gives no reference syntax, ownership, permission, symlink, size or text-decoding rules.
open_points.question: What references are valid, how are secret files opened safely, and how are their bytes converted into an HTTP header value?
options: Allow only absolute regular owner-only files opened without following symlinks, with a fixed byte and encoding rule
Allow any host path readable by the kernel
Use an external secret-provider identifier
open_points.default_guess: Allow only an explicitly bounded regular owner-owned file opened without following symlinks, interpreted as one UTF-8 header value with no trimming.

open_points.subject: Data-directory privacy checks
open_points.text: A18 says the data directory and everything in it are “private to the kernel's user” and that startup refuses otherwise, without defining ownership, mode, ACL, parent-directory or newly created-file requirements.
open_points.question: What exact filesystem properties satisfy “private”, and does the kernel create a missing data directory or require it to exist?
options: Require an existing owner-controlled directory and owner-only files/directories with no ACL access
Create it with fixed secure modes when absent
Rely on process umask and ordinary OS permissions
open_points.default_guess: Require or securely create an owner-controlled directory, enforce explicit owner-only modes, reject ACL access and symlinks, and create all children with fixed secure modes.

open_points.subject: Global store order
open_points.text: K-17 says records have one store order and several identities and list orders depend on it, but no order is defined for multiple records committed by one transaction.
open_points.question: How are positions assigned among records created in the same store call, and is the order global across all record types or separate per type?
options: Use one persisted global sequence with a documented order inside each call
Use per-table sequences
Treat records in one transaction as having the same position
open_points.default_guess: Use one persisted global sequence and assign positions in documented logical dependency order inside each call.

open_points.subject: Release upgrade and admission validity
open_points.text: A20 permits a new release to change pinned Python dependencies and the sandbox runtime, while implementation identity and AdmissionVerdict contain no release or runtime identity and existing activations continue serving.
open_points.question: After a release changes the interpreter or standard library, do existing admission verdicts and activations remain valid without rerunning their corpora?
options: Scope verdicts to the sandbox runtime and require readmission
Guarantee runtime compatibility and keep all verdicts valid
Refuse startup when stored activations were admitted under another runtime
open_points.default_guess: Scope admission validity to a release/runtime digest and require readmission before execution under a changed runtime.

open_points.subject: Release upgrade and non-contract ceilings
open_points.text: A20 says old contract resource bounds survive lowered ceilings, but says nothing about already stored implementations, constants, values, trial fixtures or flow versions that exceed newly lowered global ceilings.
open_points.question: Which existing artifacts are grandfathered after a release lowers a non-contract ceiling, and which later actions using them are refused?
options: Grandfather every persisted artifact and apply new ceilings only to newly entering bytes
Refuse startup until oversized artifacts are migrated
Apply current ceilings whenever an artifact is used, even if it was previously valid
open_points.default_guess: Grandfather persisted artifacts and apply new ceilings only when new content enters, while still enforcing current runtime response and spool ceilings.

open_points.subject: HTTP api_base_url and authority
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute http or https URL with a host, while A09 concatenates its text with the operation path and constructs Host from its authority “exactly as the manifest writes it”. Query, fragment, userinfo, encoded host, base path and authority forms are not constrained.
open_points.question: Which components and textual forms are allowed in api_base_url, and how are the final URL and Host header formed for each allowed form?
options: Allow only scheme, canonical host, optional port and optional normalized base path; forbid userinfo, query and fragment
Allow every absolute URL accepted by the HTTP library
Require an origin-only URL with no path beyond /
open_points.default_guess: Allow scheme, canonical host, optional port and a normalized base path; reject userinfo, query, fragment and ambiguous encodings.

open_points.subject: Plain-HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: A09 allows plain HTTP when the api_base_url “host is a loopback address” but does not say whether this means a literal IP, a hostname resolving to loopback, or which IPv4 and IPv6 textual forms count.
open_points.question: How is loopback determined, and is the result bound to the address actually connected to so DNS changes cannot alter the decision?
options: Permit only canonical literal loopback IP addresses
Resolve the hostname and require every result to be loopback
Permit names such as localhost based on their text
open_points.default_guess: Permit only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses parsed by one specified IP parser.

open_points.subject: Multipart port-name serialization
open_points.text: A09 inserts an unrestricted port name into Content-Disposition name and filename quoted parameters, but defines neither an escaping rule nor a refusal for quotes, control characters or non-ASCII names.
open_points.question: Which port names can be serialized safely into multipart headers, and are unsafe names escaped or refused when the binding is proposed?
options: Restrict multipart-used port names to a safe ASCII token grammar
Define a precise quoted-string escaping and encoding rule
Insert names verbatim
open_points.default_guess: Refuse bindings whose multipart port names are not safe ASCII tokens.

open_points.subject: HTTP request shape versus port cardinality
open_points.text: A09 checks path and query compatibility using value_schema type but does not combine it with M01 cardinality. A many path port is accepted by declaration yet always supplies a list, and a many port whose element schema is array can produce a list of lists that the query rule cannot encode.
open_points.question: Which cardinality and schema combinations are legal for path placeholders and GET/DELETE query parameters?
options: Path ports must be cardinality one; query rules validate the actual scalar/list shape induced by cardinality
Permit these bindings and fail them at send time
Flatten nested lists when encoding queries
open_points.default_guess: Require path ports to be cardinality one and reject every query-port declaration whose runtime shape cannot be encoded by rule 2.

open_points.subject: JSON request Content-Type and empty bodies
open_points.text: A09 says POST, PUT and PATCH inputs form a JSON object body and A10 says a request with a body has content-type and content-length, but no exact JSON Content-Type is stated and it is unclear whether an operation with no non-path inputs sends {} or no body.
open_points.question: What exact body and Content-Type are sent for a non-multipart POST, PUT or PATCH, including when no fields remain after path substitution?
options: Always send canonical JSON, including {}, with Content-Type application/json
Omit the body and its headers when the object would be empty
Let the HTTP client choose the Content-Type
open_points.default_guess: Always send the canonical JSON object, including {}, with Content-Type application/json and no parameters.

open_points.subject: Multipart boundary
open_points.text: A10 intentionally excludes the multipart boundary from the approved request description, but neither A09 nor A10 defines how the wire boundary is chosen or how collision with file or value content is prevented.
open_points.question: How is a multipart boundary generated and validated while preserving the rule that equal parts have the same approval request_digest?
options: Generate a fresh unpredictable boundary and reject or regenerate on collision
Derive a deterministic boundary from the parts
Use the HTTP library's boundary without checking
open_points.default_guess: Generate a fresh fixed-length boundary, verify it does not occur in any part body, and keep it outside request_digest as specified.

open_points.subject: HTTP transport deadline
open_points.text: A09 requires that a response “arrived within transport_timeout_ms”, but does not define when the deadline starts, whether it covers DNS, connection, TLS, headers and the full body, or whether any phase resets it.
open_points.question: What interval does transport_timeout_ms bound, and how is a timeout classified when headers or part of a body have already arrived?
options: One absolute deadline from invocation start through complete response body
Separate full timeout for each transport phase
Timeout only until final response headers
open_points.default_guess: Use one absolute monotonic deadline covering DNS through the complete bounded response body; after any request byte is written, expiry is possibly-sent.

open_points.subject: Service error bodies and credential secrecy
open_points.text: A09 retains an excerpt of an error response body as failure_detail, while A17 says a credential never enters failure_detail. A service can echo the credential it received in its error body, and no redaction or discard rule is given.
open_points.question: How can the kernel guarantee that a service-echoed credential is never persisted in failure_detail?
options: Never persist service error bodies
Remove exact credential occurrences before retaining an excerpt
Keep the excerpt and weaken the no-credential invariant
open_points.default_guess: Do not persist service error bodies; retain only bounded transport/status diagnostics generated by the kernel.

open_points.subject: Failure-detail decoding
open_points.text: A09 may retain bytes from an arbitrary HTTP error body, while M23 models failure_detail as text and A20 truncates it at a UTF-8 character boundary.
open_points.question: How are non-UTF-8 error-body bytes converted to failure_detail before bounded truncation?
options: Decode strict UTF-8 and omit the detail on failure
Decode UTF-8 with replacement
Encode arbitrary bytes as bounded base64 or hexadecimal text
open_points.default_guess: Decode UTF-8 with replacement and then truncate at a UTF-8 character boundary.

open_points.subject: Run spool byte accounting
open_points.text: A15 limits “a run whose spooled files together” while A18 says equal bytes are stored once and M22 treats files from different attempts as different SpooledFiles even when their content digests match.
open_points.question: Does spool_run_bytes_max count logical bytes for every SpooledFile occurrence or only physically unique stored bytes, and do files from a failed current attempt count before they are discarded?
options: Count every logical SpooledFile occurrence, including current-attempt files
Count unique physical content bytes only
Count only files named by committed SpooledFile records
open_points.default_guess: Count every logical produced-file occurrence, including tentative files of the current attempt, regardless of physical deduplication.

open_points.subject: Direct not_applied outcomes
open_points.text: A09 maps a non-read 4xx response to NodeExecution operation_refused and EffectAttempt not_applied, which A13 treats as a terminal node failure; A10 and M26 also discuss sending again after any not_applied attempt under a fresh approval, but no action reopens this failed element.
open_points.question: Can an owner retry an effect in the same run after a direct 4xx not_applied outcome, and if so what action creates the fresh approval?
options: A direct 4xx is terminal for that run and only a new run may try again
The element moves to owner_approval just like an unknown resolved not_applied
Add an explicit owner retry action
open_points.default_guess: Treat the direct 4xx as terminal for that run; only the resolution path reopens an element.

open_points.subject: Fresh approval after not_applied across runs
open_points.text: K-08 says the kernel “never repeats an effect without a fresh approval” and that sending one again after not_applied needs fresh approval for every class, while A12 explicitly does not deduplicate runs and A10's resend_after_not_applied test is defined only from an element's attempts within one run.
open_points.question: Does the fresh-approval requirement apply when a new run produces the same idempotency key after a prior run ended not_applied, especially for draft-write or granted nodes?
options: Apply it only to retries of the same run element
Apply it across runs by idempotency key
Treat every new run as new authority even for the same key
open_points.default_guess: Limit it to retries of the same run element, because no cross-run repeat index is modeled.

open_points.subject: Cancellation during active advancement
open_points.text: A14 permits cancelling any run that has not ended, but A18 handles requests one at a time and A13 advances synchronously until the run rests or ends, so a cancel request cannot be processed while a run is actively executing.
open_points.question: Is cancellation intended to interrupt an in-progress sandbox or HTTP execution, or can it cancel only a run already resting between requests?
options: Cancellation applies only to resting runs
Allow an out-of-band cancellation signal despite serialized surface requests
Poll queued cancellation requests between node elements
open_points.default_guess: Cancellation applies only to a run resting between requests; it does not interrupt the request currently advancing it.
